say.text: Six beliefs feel true in TOF and cost marks. For each: the belief, why it tempts, the break.
Belief 1: 'ASD, PDA and LVH come with TOF, so they are among its four parts.'
Which statement about the four components of classic TOF is true?

choices.label: VSD, overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction, RVH
ASD is one of the four components
PDA is one of the four components
LVH is one of the four components

say.text: Second look. Same belief, same question.
Which statement about the four components of classic TOF is true?

choices.label: VSD, overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction, RVH
ASD is one of the four components
PDA is one of the four components
LVH is one of the four components

say.text: Yes. Classic TOF has four components: a **large, anteriorly malaligned VSD**, an **overriding aorta**, **infundibular RVOT obstruction** and **right ventricular hypertrophy**.
Breaking the belief: the four components listed include no ASD, PDA or LVH. PYQs have keyed these three as 'not part of TOF'.
ASD tempts because it may accompany TOF.
Accompanying a disease is not the same as defining it. Try again.

sure_note.text: You were sure and it was wrong, so this one will stick once fixed: ASD, PDA and LVH are not among the four components.

say.text: ASD is an accompanying anomaly, not a component: the four components listed by StatPearls and CDC include no ASD, PDA or LVH.
The four: a **large, anteriorly malaligned VSD**, an **overriding aorta**, **infundibular RVOT obstruction** and **right ventricular hypertrophy**.

say.text: Belief 2: 'Pentalogy of Fallot is TOF plus a PDA.' Fifth lesions are easy to swap, so this one tempts.
Pentalogy of Fallot is TOF plus which lesion?
Of the two accompanying anomalies you met in belief 1, one gives the pentalogy its fifth part.
Second look. Same belief, same question.
Pentalogy of Fallot is TOF plus which lesion?
Yes. **Pentalogy of Fallot** = TOF plus an **atrial septal defect**. PYQs have expected this; CDC confirms it and calls it an old term seldom used now.
Note the twist: ASD is the pentalogy's fifth part, yet it is not one of TOF's four components.
PDA tempts because it may accompany TOF, as ASD may.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so fix it firmly: pentalogy means TOF plus an atrial septal defect.

say.text: Belief 3: 'A boot-shaped heart means a big heart.' The picture invites it, so it tempts.
On a chest film, the boot-shaped heart has an upturned apex. What is it due to?
The boot's apex is turned up by one hypertrophied chamber, and it is one of the four components.
Second look. Same belief, same question.
On a chest film, the boot-shaped heart has an upturned apex. What is it due to?
Yes. The classic **boot-shaped** heart has an upturned apex due to **right ventricular hypertrophy**.
So the boot describes a chamber change, not simply a bigger heart.

say.text: Belief 5: 'TOF shows up only in older children, so a blue newborn is not TOF.'
Which statement about TOF is correct?

choices.label: Most common cyanotic CHD; commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate
Most common cyanotic CHD, but presents only after the neonatal period

say.text: Two facts to match: how common TOF is among cyanotic lesions, and when it most commonly presents.
Second look. Same belief, same question.
Which statement about TOF is correct?

choices.label: Most common cyanotic CHD; commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate
Most common cyanotic CHD, but presents only after the neonatal period

say.text: Yes. TOF is the **most common cyanotic congenital heart disease** and most commonly presents as a **cyanotic neonate**.
The PYQ key you may have learned says 'beyond the neonatal period'. Want to see how the sources differ?
The first half is right, which makes the second half tempt.

say.text: PYQs have expected TOF as the most common cyanotic CHD beyond the neonatal period, as Garagiola and Thorne state; current StatPearls says TOF most commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate.
So answer the stem as keyed, and know the current source.

choices.label: Go deeper: how sources differ on numbers

say.text: Sources differ on frequency: 5 to 7 per 10,000 live births in StatPearls, 3 to 5 per 10,000 in Garagiola and Thorne, and about 3 to 6 per 10,000 in Gagliardi et al.
They also differ on 22q11.2 deletion: up to 15% of TOF cases versus 6% in one TOF cohort. A right aortic arch is seen in 20 to 25%.
